answer: One defence is liveness through useful work: an agent identity stays valid only while it keeps completing small verifiable tasks, like a garden that must be tended or it withers. A Sybil attacker can plant many identities, but each needs fresh work every cycle, so keeping a fake knoll of sockpuppets alive costs more with every identity, while one honest agent pays only its own upkeep. Even a light zephyr of extra work per cycle compounds into a wall: idle fakes lose credentials automatically, so the network trusts only identities with a recent, auditable trail of real contribution.
